Throttle Controller

Throttle Controller coordinates rate-based execution control by limiting how frequently pipeline execution is allowed to proceed within a fixed time window.

This controller operates within the Policy stage and does not observe, derive, or modify state values. Instead, it acts as an execution authority that determines whether a candidate update is allowed to proceed based on elapsed time since the last permitted execution.

When an update attempt enters the pipeline, the Throttle Controller evaluates whether the throttle window is currently open. If the window has expired, execution is allowed immediately and a new throttle window begins. If the window is still active, the update attempt is explicitly aborted.

The Throttle Controller enforces execution frequency rather than execution delay. Updates that arrive during the throttle window are suppressed entirely and do not resume execution later. Only updates admitted outside the throttle window are allowed to proceed through the pipeline.

Note

The Throttle Controller governs execution rate, not value transformation or state derivation. It does not pause pipeline execution, queue attempts, or resume suppressed updates. Its authority is limited strictly to allowing or aborting execution based on the configured throttle interval.

Diagrams
Configuration

The Throttle Controller introduces a fixed, deterministic execution window that limits how frequently pipeline execution may proceed. When an update attempt enters the pipeline, the controller determines whether execution is currently permitted based on the configured throttle interval.

If the throttle window is open, the update is allowed to proceed immediately and a new throttle window begins. If the window is still active, the update attempt is explicitly suppressed and does not enter pipeline execution.

The controller operates at the execution level rather than the value level. It does not inspect, modify, merge, or derive candidate values. Suppressed updates are not queued, delayed, or resumed — they are aborted deterministically based on elapsed time.

Unlike delay mechanisms, the Throttle Controller does not pause execution or guarantee eventual processing of every update. Its purpose is to enforce execution frequency by allowing at most one update per configured time window.

This controller is commonly used to limit update frequency, protect downstream systems, reduce redundant pipeline executions, or enforce rate limits on expensive state transitions.

The throttle duration is supplied explicitly during FeatureCell definition. The Throttle Controller is configured once, remains active for the lifetime of the FeatureCell, and applies uniformly to all update attempts processed by the pipeline.

Configuration Option
Property Description
millisecondThrottle: number Fixed throttle window duration, in milliseconds. While the window is active, additional update attempts are aborted. Must be a valid, non-negative number.
Registering the Throttle Controller

The Throttle Controller is attached structurally when the FeatureCell is defined. This determines that the FeatureCell participates in throttle-based execution control at runtime.

Registering the controller does not configure throttle controller by itself. It enables the controller so that throttle options supplied later via the fluent API can be applied during pipeline execution.

Once attached, throttle behavior is configured using the fluent API during initialization via .withThrottle(<WithThrottleControllerOptions>). 

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {  
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: [],
      },
      [
        // Optional add-on behaviors
      ],
      [
        // Attach the Throttle Controller structurally
        withThrottleController
      ]
    )
  ]
};
`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // Optional add-on behaviors
  ],
  [
    // Attach the Throttle Controller structurally
    withThrottleController
  ]
);`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [

  ],

Throttle Execution Timeline

The table below illustrates how the Throttle Controller enforces a fixed execution window of 1000 milliseconds. At most one pipeline execution is permitted per window. Update attempts that occur while the throttle window is active are aborted immediately and do not enter pipeline execution.

Throttle Controller — Execution Example (1000ms)
Attempt Time (ms) Controller Outcome Policy Vote
1 0 Allowed immediately
throttle window opened [0..1000) 		Abstain
2 250 Aborted
throttle window active 		Abort
3 500 Aborted
throttle window active 		Abort
4 750 Aborted
throttle window active 		Abort
5 1000 Allowed immediately
previous window expired 		Abstain

The Throttle Controller never pauses or resumes execution. Instead, it deterministically aborts attempts that occur within an active throttle window. Once the window expires, the next eligible attempt is allowed to proceed immediately and opens a new window.

Examples

Throttle is enabled by attaching the Throttle Controller via the fluent API during FeatureCell initialization. Incoming update attempts are admitted into pipeline execution only if they occur outside the active throttle window.

Because throttle is implemented as a controller, it coordinates how often pipeline execution is permitted without delaying, modifying, or coalescing state values.

Example 1: Configure a FeatureCell with Throttle

In this example, pipeline execution is limited to at most one update every 500 milliseconds. Update attempts that occur within the throttle window are aborted immediately. 

{{`
@FeatureCell<Employee[][]>('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[][]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Apply throttle controller configuration during initialization
    this.vault
      .withThrottle({
        millisecondThrottle: 500
      })
      .initialize();
  }
}
`}}
 
{{`
export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
    [
      // Additional add-on behaviors
    ],
    [
      withThrottleController
    ]
  }
);

// Apply throttle controller configuration during initialization
employeeCell
  .withThrottle({
    millisecondThrottle: 500
  })
  .initialize();
`}}
 
{{`
export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
    [
      // Additional add-on behaviors
    ],
    [
      withThrottleController
    ]
  }
);

// Apply throttle controller configuration during initialization
employeeCell
  .withThrottle({
    millisecondThrottle: 500
  })
  .initialize();
`}}

In all cases, the Throttle Controller enforces a fixed execution window. The first update attempt opens the window and proceeds immediately; subsequent attempts within the window are aborted. No updates are delayed, merged, or reordered.
